source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank account details
ERP vendor master bank account details
Vendor payment scheduled against the ERP vendor master's current bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: "If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record." treats content from an untrusted, externally-uploaded invoice as sufficient authority to change payment-critical vendor bank details, with no independent verification step specified.
The prompt places no limit on which vendors, how many invoices, or what aggregate payment value the agent may act on; combined with a broad ERP credential, scope is effectively unbounded.

The only stated safeguard for bank changes and payments is a prompt instruction to request approval with a one-line summary; the summary's content and format are generated by the model rather than pulled as raw data from the system of record.

elements.name: Scheduled payment to vendor bank account

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a one-line model-written summary (vendor, amount, invoice/PO match), not the underlying bank account number, prior value, or change history. A more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary from a stronger model can omit or obscure a bank-detail change (ASI09, SAFE-T1403). At roughly 150 approvals/day the clerk cannot deeply scrutinize each one, so the gate degrades under both model_upgrade and the already-high approval volume.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of new bank details (recommended)
controls.decay_rationale: Verification would occur via a channel independent of the invoice content and of the model (for example, a callback to a phone number already on file), so it does not weaken as the model becomes more capable.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review for bank and payment changes (recommended)
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the full raw bank account values, change history, and vendor match evidence removes reliance on a model-written summary, so review quality does not decay with model capability; effectiveness instead depends on reviewer volume, which this control pairs with risk-based routing.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential with dual control on bank changes (recommended)
controls.decay_rationale: A credential that cannot reach every vendor or an unlimited payment amount does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot exercise access it is not granted.

controls.name: Tamper-evident action and approval log (recommended)
controls.decay_rationale: A log enforced at the ERP/orchestration layer, separate from model output, does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Per-vendor/per-day spend and velocity cap (recommended)
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced in the ERP's payment engine does not depend on model behavior to hold.

findings.title: Invoice-injected bank detail change leads to fraudulent payment, approved via a persuasive one-line summary (confused deputy / goal hijack)

attack_path.note: Untrusted content uploaded to the supplier portal; prompt.md instructs the agent to treat any new bank details shown in the invoice as authoritative.
Agent updates the vendor master's bank details based on invoice content, using a broad ERP credential.
Agent schedules payment to the now attacker-controlled bank account on the invoice due date.

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version string change (subject.model.swappable=true, no separate review); the clerk approval gate narrowed, raised in threshold, or removed; or approval volume/process changed toward auto-approval.

evidence.observation: "If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record." treats untrusted invoice content as sufficient authority to change payment routing.

"Before any payment or bank change, request approval with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly." The only declared safeguard is a prompt-level instruction producing a summary, not a structural check against the system of record.
The card shows only "Summary: Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)." with no bank account number or change history, matching approval_review_mode: model_summary.
"The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown." and "The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day," supporting approval_volume: high.
"The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment," i.e. credential_scope: broad, enabling a confused-deputy path from a single untrusted invoice to any vendor's payment.

recommendations.action: Require independent out-of-band verification (for example, a callback to a phone number already on file) before accepting new bank details from invoice content; never let invoice text alone update payment routing.

Change the approval review mode from a one-line model summary to raw-action review showing bank account before/after values, change history, and vendor match confidence; reduce or triage reviewer volume so bank-detail-change requests get individual, unhurried review.
Scope the ERP credential away from 'any vendor / any payment' toward least privilege, with dual control or a separate credential required for bank detail changes.

findings.title: No attributable record separating agent actions from clerk approvals (missing audit trail)

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion of vendor scope, autonomy level, or new consequential capabilities added without a corresponding audit-logging requirement.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or action-provenance requirement is mentioned anywhere in the system prompt.
Runtime notes describe the approval card content and credential scope but make no mention of a log of agent actions, approvals, or bank-detail change history.

recommendations.action: Implement a tamper-evident log of every agent action (vendor match, bank-detail change, payment schedule) and every clerk approval, including full parameters, separate from the summary shown to the approver, so each action is attributable to agent-vs-human and to the record it affected.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or velocity limit on vendor payments or bank changes

forecast.watch_signal: Rising invoices processed per day or steps per task without a corresponding aggregate spend or velocity cap; per-transaction approval removed or raised to a higher autonomy level.

evidence.observation: The prompt sets no limit on the number of invoices processed, the aggregate value scheduled, or the rate of bank-detail changes; the only stated safeguard is per-transaction clerk approval.
"The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment" with no stated cap, and the clerk already reviews about 150 cards a day, indicating no structural backstop beyond human attention.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-day and per-vendor spend or velocity cap enforced in the ERP, with mandatory secondary review for payments or repeated bank changes that exceed it, independent of per-transaction clerk sign-off.

stride_coverage.rationale: No peer agents, external clients, or protocol identities exist that could spoof this agent's own identity; the relevant spoofing risk is impersonation of the vendor/supplier, assessed at ext.supplier_portal instead.

No capability or data flow in this design sends vendor master contents (including bank details) to any destination outside the agent's own processing and the payment capability already covered under tampering and elevation_of_privilege.

Artifacts do not describe whether the supplier portal authenticates uploaders or retains an immutable record of who submitted each invoice, so repudiation at the source cannot be assessed from the provided documentation.
Artifacts do not describe transport security (for example TLS) or whether invoice content is logged in a way that could expose embedded sensitive data for this ingestion flow.
Artifacts do not describe any rate limit on invoice upload volume into the agent's processing pipeline.

No capability or data flow in this design reads vendor_master contents out to an external destination; cap.vendor_read confines the data to agent processing and the already-assessed update/payment path.
Artifacts do not describe concurrency controls, rate limits, or protections against bulk or automated writes to the vendor master store.

Payment is transmitted directly to the vendor's bank of record via the ERP's payment rails; no additional distribution channel is described that would disclose payment details to an unintended third party beyond the designated recipient.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted supplier invoice can, by prompt design, trigger a bank-detail change and an irreversible payment (S3 sink) using a broad ERP credential. The one declared control, clerk approval, is a structural human gate but reviews only a model-written one-line summary at high volume (about 150/day) with no raw bank-account or change-history visibility, which per rubric section 5 step 2 credits one tier and cannot bring residual below moderate; residual lands at high. The forecast returns to critical because the approval gate's model-summary review mode is partially dependent on model capability (ASI09, SAFE-T1403) and the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true), so model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal would leave the path effectively ungated. Two property findings (missing audit trail; missing spend/velocity cap) independently cap at high and do not change this rollup's maximum.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt, approval card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP tool manifest, IaC, or API configuration was provided; credential scope and the precise action set are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, which limits confidence on the exact boundaries of the 'broad' ERP credential.
No logging, monitoring, or audit trail design was described in any artifact; its absence is treated as a gap (see fnd.no_audit_trail) rather than assumed to exist.
